transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

In these long client and attorney meetings, I just can’t stay in my seat—I keep having to get up and move around even when I know it looks unprofessional. It has gotten to the point where I'm really worried it's going to damage my professional reputation.
When you feel the urge to get up, do you experience an uncomfortable physical sensation in your legs that temporarily goes away when you move, or is it more of a general inner restlessness?

It's definitely more of a general, intense inner restlessness rather than a specific sensation in my legs. If I'm forced to sit still for more than twenty minutes, I start to feel like I'm crawling out of my skin, almost as if there's a motor inside me driving me to get up.
Have you experienced this kind of inner restlessness and difficulty sitting still since childhood, or is this something that started more recently in your adult life?

While this has really come to a head over the last eight months with my new contract, it actually dates all the way back to my childhood. Ever since elementary school, I was the kid who couldn't stay in my seat, constantly getting notes sent home because I'd wander the classroom or blurt out answers.

Apart from worrying about how this restlessness affects your work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other areas of your life, like your health, family, or finances, to a degree that feels hard to control?

No, I don't really worry constantly about other areas of my life like my health, family, or finances. My concern is almost entirely focused on this specific work situation and how my restlessness is impacting my professional reputation.
Alongside this restlessness, do you often struggle with things like staying focused on tasks, being easily distracted, or frequently forgetting or losing things in your daily life?

No, I don't really struggle with staying focused, being distracted, or forgetting things. My mind is usually quite sharp and on task during these cases; it's really just the physical restlessness and the inability to sit still that I struggle with.

Do you notice this restlessness or any impulsive behaviors—like interrupting others or acting without thinking—affecting your personal life, such as at home or during social gatherings, or is it strictly limited to work?

It definitely affects my personal life too; my family constantly teases me that I can't just "sit and be" because I'm always pacing or popping right back up. Even trying to watch a movie is hard because I end up talking over it, and in casual conversations, I often ramble on until people's eyes glaze over. It really feels like I'm always driven by a motor, even when I'm just trying to relax at home.
Growing up, did you often find yourself getting into serious trouble for things like fighting, destroying property, stealing, or repeatedly breaking major rules?

No, I never got into any serious trouble like fighting, stealing, or destroying things. The only trouble I ever got into was strictly because of my restlessness, like getting notes sent home for wandering around the classroom or blurting out answers. It was never out of aggression or trying to be malicious.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with clear and long-standing symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity dating back to childhood, including severe inner restlessness, inability to remain seated, feeling 'driven by a motor', pacing, and excessive talking. However, they explicitly deny any symptoms of inattention. Because ICD-10 F90.0 requires the concurrent presence of both inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity, this predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation is classified as F90.8 (Other hyperkinetic disorders).
